text:
maria: Heads-up — after the continuous-batcher rollout to 60% yesterday we saw a latency spike on the small-req path and overall throughput drop ~12% on prod-GPU pools. Not good.

akshay: saw it in grafana too, p50 jumped ~40ms on 8k request runway. Any correlating deploys?

maria: rollout was the only change. PR #4142 changed token_budget_target from 64->32 and added a new priority classifier that groups small requests more aggressively.

sara: @maria do you have profiler traces?

maria: pasted a short perf dump below (sampled tails from a hot pod):

```
# top spans (hot path)
batcher.cpp:213::form_batch  48%  (esp when queue depth 4-12)
kernel_selector.cpp::choose_kernel  22%  (fallback to fp16_gemm on short seqs)
kv_cache.cpp::lookup 12%  (high miss rate -> eviction churn)
memcpy 8%  (device->host sync on fallback path)
```

maria: I also see logs where the batcher marks a group as HIGH_PRIORITY and forces immediate flush even when under budget. That increases kernel selector churn.

jon: can you paste the queue policy config?

maria: snippet:

```
continuous_batcher {
  token_budget_target: 32
  max_wait_ms: 12
  priority_classifier: "aggressive-small-reqs-v2"
  queue_policy: FIFO_WITH_PRIORITY
}
```

devon: looks like aggressive classifier is favoring small requests into many tiny batches -> kernel selector keeps toggling between small-kernel and standard-kernel, causing expensive context switches.

akshay: do we have metrics on kernel selection flips? maybe log counts of choose_kernel decisions.

logbot: [automated] kernel_selector.choose_kernel flips increased 6.3x after rollout. Top affected node: prod-GPU-pool-7.

maria: KV cache metrics are ugly too — miss rate up from 3% -> 17% for short conversational flows. Likely because we evict earlier due to more aggressive batching and earlier flushes.

sara: eviction churn could explain memcpy spikes (evict -> reload -> device transfers). Do we see increased device memory pressure?

maria: yes, OOM pressure events are 2x and we see fallback offloading to host more often.

jon: Which customers hit this? Any Dedicated tenants?

maria: two Dedicated customers on that pool reported increased tail latency and saw throughput drop. One opened a support ticket.

akshay: quick hypothesis: lowering token_budget_target reduced batch size, classifier prioritization fragmented batches, causing kernel selection oscillation + KV thrash. Net effect: less token throughput and higher latency.

devon: agree. Fix options: rollback config to previous target 64, or tune classifier to be less eager (probabilistic sampling), or increase max_wait_ms to allow batches to build.

maria: I ran a quick A/B on canary and raising max_wait_ms to 30ms reduced p50 by ~25ms and smoothed kernel flips. But throughput still down ~4%.

akshay: can we add a short-term mitigation: when kernel_selector detects >N flips within T seconds, mark the classifier as muted for that model and fall back to size-based batching? (circuit for oscillation)

jon: code change is straightforward but riskier. For immediate relief: rollback rollout to 20% and revert token_budget_target to 64.

ops-bot: rollback scheduled? React with :white_check_mark: to approve.

sara: +1 rollback. Also set alert on kernel_selector.flip_rate > 3/min.

devon: I'm happy to own the flip-rate alert and the short-term rollback. Will run perf traces pre/post.

maria: I'll open a follow-up ticket to rework the priority classifier with a stability objective (minimize kernel flips and KV churn) — linking perf harness and dataset.

akshay: useful logs to collect if we don't rollback: kernel selection counts, batch sizes distribution, kv cache miss/evict per model, device mem pressure, memcpy hotspots. Also capture a few full perf traces.

maria: created ticket INF-2213 and attached canary traces + grafana panels.

jon: timeline?

devon: rolling rollback now to 20% -> monitoring.

logbot: [automated] rollback applied to rollout controller for continuous-batcher. Old token_budget_target restored to 64 on 40% of nodes.

maria: after rollback p50 trending back down; kernel_selector flips back to baseline. I'll keep watching the kv miss rate.

akshay: nice work. Long-term we should add a stability metric into the rollout gating (kernel flip rate + kv miss delta).

sara: agree — adding to RFC for next heuristic iteration.

maria: thanks team. I'll post a short postmortem once INF-2213 has full analysis.

jon: thumbs up :thumbsup:
